newsitem.title: LATVIA: INTERVIEW-RIGAS KOMMERCBANKA SAYS BANK MERGERS NEEDED.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-RIGAS KOMMERCBANKA SAYS BANK MERGERS NEEDED.

text.p: Third-largest bank Rigas kommercbanka (RKB) said on Monday that the Latvian banking system needed mergers and that the company was also in favour of linking up with another bank.
But bank president Vladimir Kulik declined to say whether RKB was in talks with other banks or what steps had been taken to carry out a merger.
Kulik also told Reuters in an interview that Rigas komercbanka had held unsuccessful talks with other leading banks to form a pan-Baltic financial institution to operate in the leasing market.
"Of course, we definitely do need that (mergers). There is no other way but I will first merge and then talk about it," he said. "In economic terms there is no alternative."
"Both the EBRD and the World Bank are saying that this is the right direction but I would say that the managerial level in banks is not yet ready for mergers," Kulik said.
He said the merger of Unibanka and Zemes Bank, cancelled suddenly last week, would have been a good idea as it would have created at least one big bank.

"I think that this is a case of lacking survival instinct. People simply do not feel the smell of burning," Kulik said, referring to the dangers of small banks competing with each other as the market changes.
Kulik also said that RKB held unsuccessful talks with other banks on forming a pan-Baltic financial institution.
"We have just finished an unsuccesful round of talks or four months of consultations with both Estonian and Lithuanian banks, different partners on both sides," Kulik said.
"I am afraid that by attempting this, Rigas komercbanka is some four to five years ahead of time," Kulik said, referring to the consultations.
